headline: A deep Pacific storm brings rain tonight and gusty southeast winds, with coastal flood warnings along the Strait of Juan de Fuca shore Tuesday, more rain Wednesday night through Thursday, and a Flood Watch for the southern Olympics and southern Puget Sound from Wednesday through Sunday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Showers are thinning out across the Sequim–Port Angeles area and the Puget Sound lowlands this afternoon, but a strong low-pressure system offshore sends a front in with widespread rain reaching the coast Monday evening and spreading inland overnight; around Seattle the rain should start between about 4 and 10 PM. Gusty southeast winds develop, strongest in the San Juan Islands, Island County and along the coast, where there is better than an 80 percent chance of gusts over 40 mph and a Wind Advisory runs until 4 PM Tuesday for the coast and western and southern Olympic foothills; Seattle sees south-southeast winds around 9–17 mph with gusts near 23 mph. Lows range from the upper 30s to mid 40s. Rising snow levels end the Olympics' Winter Weather Advisory at 4 PM, but a Winter Weather Advisory runs from 8 PM tonight to 10 PM Tuesday for the Whatcom and Skagit County Cascades.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Rain continues Tuesday before the front moves out Tuesday evening, leaving lingering showers and breezy winds. Another system brings a fresh round of widespread rain and breezy winds Wednesday night into early Thursday, with snow levels rising well above the passes by Wednesday evening, so the mountains get rain rather than snow. A Flood Watch runs from Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon for the Olympics and their western and southern foothills, southern Hood Canal, Olympia and the southern Puget Sound, the middle Chehalis River valley, and the Willapa and Black Hills; the Skokomish River will likely reach flood stage around midweek and could rise to moderate or even near major flooding, though no widespread river flooding is expected. Temperatures run above normal through Wednesday night, with highs in the low to mid 50s and lows well into the 40s.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Thursday's system moves out by evening but may first bring another round of gusty winds and widespread rain that could be moderate to heavy at times. Unsettled weather lingers into Friday, then high pressure may build over the weekend for a brief change to quieter weather, though forecasters are not yet sure how strong it will be or exactly where it sets up. Temperatures return closer to normal from Friday on.

coast: High surf combined with high tides brings hazardous coastal conditions, including major coastal flooding, peaking Tuesday and lasting into the second half of the week, with another peak Thursday. On Tuesday, Coastal Flood Warnings run from 8 AM to 3 PM for the eastern and western Strait of Juan de Fuca (including the Sequim–Port Angeles shore), the north Washington coast and the Grays Harbor County coast, and from 2 AM to 4 PM for San Juan County; a Coastal Flood Advisory runs from 2 AM to 5 PM Tuesday for the Seattle, Shoreline–Lynnwood–Everett, Island County, Pierce and south King, Skagit–Snohomish and Whatcom shorelines. Tides become a concern for the inland shorelines from Wednesday, with Coastal Flood Watches from late Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon and again from late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon covering the Strait, Port Townsend, Puget Sound from Seattle to Everett, eastern Kitsap County, Hood Canal, the San Juans, Island County and the coast. A High Surf Advisory covers the north Washington and Grays Harbor coasts from 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM Wednesday. For boaters, a Storm Warning covers the outer coastal waters (10–60 miles out) and Gale Warnings cover the inner coastal waters and both the west and east entrances of the Strait until 11 PM Tuesday; Small Craft Advisories cover the central Strait until 7 AM Tuesday (with a brief overnight lull before winds pick back up Tuesday) and Admiralty Inlet, the northern inland waters and San Juan Islands, and the Grays Harbor bar until 11 PM Tuesday. Another front Wednesday into Thursday could bring even stronger winds, likely more storm warnings on the outer waters and small craft to gale conditions elsewhere, with isolated afternoon thunderstorms possible over the coastal waters each day. Seas of 10–15 feet this afternoon build to 18–25 feet by Tuesday afternoon, ease slightly but turn into longer-period swells Wednesday and Thursday, and drop below 10 feet Friday night into Saturday before building again to 8–12 feet by the end of the weekend; Friday brings a brief break from the wind before more windy systems next week.
watch_for: Coastal flooding at Tuesday's high tide along the Strait of Juan de Fuca (warning 8 AM–3 PM) and Puget Sound shorelines, with more coastal flood watches Wednesday and Thursday.
The Skokomish River, likely reaching flood stage midweek and possibly moderate to near-major flooding, under a Flood Watch from Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon.
Whether high pressure really builds this weekend; its strength and placement are still uncertain.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the wet, windy, stormy pattern with coastal flooding through Friday, but have low confidence in how strong and where the weekend high pressure sets up.
